definition: When shooting live-action reference for characters of different physical scale than the performer (a full-sized adult standing in for a dwarf or child character), have the performer adjust their OWN posture to match the target's height (e.g. walking on their knees) to get correct eyelines and on-screen composition — while accepting that the resulting movement TIMING will read wrong, and capturing accurate timing separately from performers at the character's true effective scale where possible.
purpose: Get a cheap, fast composition/eyeline reference immediately, from whatever crew is on hand, while being explicit that the same reference is NOT valid evidence for timing — rather than either skipping composition reference entirely or mistakenly trusting the knee-walking take's timing.
visible_effect: A knee-walking performer's on-screen framing and sightlines match what the smaller character would actually produce, while their pace of movement (how long it takes to cross a given distance) does not match the target character's true timing at all.
psychological_or_gameplay_effect: None directly — a production reference technique; its value is entirely in what it lets the team validate cheaply, not in anything an audience ever sees.
physical_interpretation: Posture substitutes for scale (a lowered eye-height and shortened effective stride approximate a smaller character's geometry) without substituting for the smaller character's own true mass/leg-length-driven timing.
use_cases: quick composition/eyeline previs for a character of significantly different scale than any available reference performer
any production wanting SOME physical reference for a differently-scaled character faster than sourcing a performer who actually matches that scale
non_use_cases: any pass whose purpose is establishing TIMING (how fast the character moves, how long an action takes) — the technique's own scale-substitution is explicitly stated to break exactly that quality
a final or near-final performance capture, where an actually-scaled performer (or a scaled/retimed version of the reference) is needed rather than the raw knee-walking take
interactions: cardboard_box_puppet_scale_proxy (this batch, video 48) — a sibling cheap-scale-proxy technique; that one sacrifices ALL motion fidelity to get scale/silhouette only, this one keeps a real human performance but sacrifices only timing to get BOTH scale-correct eyelines and (unreliable) motion

physical_reference_timing_method (W01) — the general principle that physical reference is a legitimate timing source; this entry is a specific, named EXCEPTION where the same general technique (shoot yourself as reference) explicitly does NOT transfer for timing, only for composition
cadence_representation: Not represented, and not really applicable: a live-action reference-shooting technique with no digital trace for Cadence to operate on. The transferable lesson — that a single reference capture can be VALID evidence for one quality (composition) while being INVALID evidence for another (timing) from the same take — has no explicit representation in this build's `evidence_status` conventions either; a knowledge entry's own evidence is treated as valid or not as a whole, with no field distinguishing 'valid for claim X, not for claim Y' within one cited source.
detection_and_measurement_methods: None — a production/reference-capture technique with no digital trace.
failure_modes: trusting a knee-walking reference take's TIMING as if it were valid, when the presenter states directly that 'one of the disadvantages of walking on your knees is you don't get a good sense of accurate timing'
skipping physical reference entirely because no correctly-scaled performer is available, losing the real composition/eyeline value this cheap substitute technique still provides
roblox_considerations: None specific — a live-action reference-capture technique independent of target engine.
examples: animators walking on their knees to represent dwarf characters specifically to 'get accurate eye lines and composition for the camera', with the explicit caveat 'you don't get a good sense of accurate timing for how long it takes to move around' (video @ 11:06–11:37)

contrasted directly in the same passage: when the actual (correctly-scaled) principal cast was available and could 'walk around freely', their takes captured accurate timing that the knee-walking stand-in takes could not (video @ 11:39–11:44)
evidence_status: video: https://youtu.be/MNinZWlhprE @ 11:06–11:44 — Erica Pinto describes the knee-walking scale-substitution technique and states its specific timing limitation directly; no frames extracted (transcript-only); experimental until validated
